source: gh repo list DareDev256 --limit 300 (all visibilities, archived excluded) merged with data/registry-curation.json

definitions.selection: hand-picked in data/registry-curation.json — not the most recently pushed, and not everything that exists
definitions.radius: curated tier: flagship > shipped > tool. NOT repository size
definitions.heat: 0 to 1 by recency of last push — 1 is today, 0 is 90 days or older
definitions.unnamed: registry entries drawn but not labelled — the count is real, the placement is arrangement
definitions.private: private repositories are counted; a private repo is named only where it is already public elsewhere on the page, and never links to code
definitions.proves: star and fork counts are substituted from the live gh call at build time, never typed by hand
definitions.archived: excluded from the graph but still counted in totals.repos

core.label: CORE
core.what: The autonomous agent that manages the rest of the registry — it reads the repos, opens the work, and reports to Discord without being asked.
core.proves: 97 modules, 60,795 lines of first-party code, running unattended on a Mac Mini.

nodes.what: The first MCP server for Final Cut Pro XML — drive a professional video timeline with natural language.
nodes.proves: 121 stars and 22 forks from developers who found it on their own. 11 releases published to PyPI.

nodes.what: Sports-betting analytics platform built for a paying client and running in production.
nodes.proves: Live at betmetrics.ca with real users and a paid engagement behind it.

nodes.what: Generates an artist website as a named world rather than a template — it derives type, colour and motion from the artist's own premise.
nodes.proves: In its one documented blind A/B, the judge asked to spot the generated site picked a hand-built one and ranked the generated site the most hand-made of five. It refuses to print a number it cannot source.

nodes.what: This site, plus a full draggable desktop OS at /os — 20 apps and 46 vanilla modules with no framework and no runtime dependencies.
nodes.proves: No UI framework and no component library — 46 vanilla modules. Every number on this page traces to a generator that exits non-zero rather than invent one.

nodes.what: Mission control for the agent — the surface that shows what it ran, what it changed, and what it is blocked on.
nodes.proves: Serving live agent telemetry daily. The public view runs on demo data so client names never leave the machine.

nodes.what: The music-video directing catalogue — the other half of the career, kept deliberately separate from the engineering surface.
nodes.proves: Live, and the source of record for the directing credits claimed on this page.

nodes.what: Content-creator and Twitch-streamer site built for a client, shipped end to end.
nodes.proves: Deployed and handed over, with contact delivery verified by receipt rather than by the page's success banner.

nodes.what: Desktop app that generates character sprite sheets — 8 directions and 100+ actions from one text prompt.
nodes.proves: A native desktop binary, not a web demo. Written in Go with a React front end.

nodes.what: macOS anti-infostealer toolkit that blocks curl-pipe-shell paste attacks and audits how far a leaked secret would reach.
nodes.proves: Written after a real ClickFix attack, not from a threat report. Defensive use only.

nodes.what: A free, open-source learning game: 60-second rounds that teach generative-AI concepts by playing them — prompt craft, hallucination hunting, red teaming.
nodes.proves: Spaced repetition on the FSRS algorithm, so retention is scheduled rather than hoped for.

nodes.what: Structured prompt builder for nine image and video engines.
nodes.proves: 10 stars and 4 forks, and it runs on its own domain.

nodes.what: Retrieval-augmented generation that will not answer without citing the passage it used.
nodes.proves: Built to make an unsourced answer structurally impossible rather than discouraged.
